title: observability: automate private installs (Prometheus/Grafana, log shipping, dashboards, alerts, terraform)
author: Marco Ruiz
release_notes: Adds automated observability stack for Private installs: Helm chart for Prometheus/Grafana, Terraform module to provision monitoring infra, bundled dashboards and alerts, log-shipping integration, and upgrade/rollback tooling. Backwards compatible and configurable via installer flags.
description:
Motivation: Private (VPC/on-prem) installs currently require manual wiring for monitoring. This PR adds an opinionated, automatable observability stack that can be enabled during install or applied to existing clusters. It includes a Helm chart (redwood-observability), Terraform modules for required infra, log-shipping via Vector/Fluent Bit, curated Grafana dashboards, Prometheus alert rules, and installer/upgrade hooks.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add infra/helm/redwood-observability chart with templates for Prometheus, Grafana, node-exporter, and a lightweight alertmanager config. Values are parameterized for retention, scrape intervals, and resource requests.
- Add terraform/private/observability module that provisions namespace, storageClass-aware PVCs for Prometheus TSDB (optional), and optional external S3-compatible remote_write configuration.
- Wire installer (installer/private/install.sh and installer/private/enable_observability.sh) to optionally deploy the chart and apply Terraform outputs for hosted customers.
- Add scripts for upgrade and rollback (scripts/upgrade/observability-upgrade.sh, scripts/rollback/observability-rollback.sh) that run helm diff, run preflight checks, and take snapshots of Prometheus TSDB when enabled.
- Add log-shipping integration using Vector (preferred) with fallback Fluent Bit config; includes parsers for Redwood logs and automatic annotation of pods.
- Add curated Grafana dashboards (dashboards/redwood-observability) focused on per-model/route token consumption, GPU/CPU utilization, disk pressure, and alert dashboards.
- Add alert rules for high scrape latency, TSDB high memory pressure, alertmanager silences on upgrade, and missing log ingestion.
- Add e2e test that runs a private install in CI using a lightweight k3s cluster and validates Prometheus/Grafana endpoints, alert firing on synthetic load, and log ingestion.

Checklist:
- [x] Helm chart with values and templates
- [x] Terraform module + examples
- [x] Installer flags and idempotent enable/disable hooks
- [x] Log shipping manifests and parsers
- [x] Dashboards and alert rules checked in
- [x] e2e smoke test added
- [x] Docs and migration guide updated

Testing and validation:
- Ran full e2e on k3s (ci/integration-e2e) — initial run was flaky due to RBAC timing; fixed by adding readiness probe gating and retry backoff. Subsequent runs passed.
- Terraform plan validated against two customer-like var sets (on-prem PVC-backed and cloud S3 remote_write).
- Performed manual upgrade test: enabled observability on a staging private cluster, applied upgrade script, and verified no alert churn and that Prometheus TSDB snapshot completed.

Backwards compatibility:
- All changes are behind an installer flag `enable_observability` (false by default). Existing private installs are unaffected unless the flag is turned on. The Helm chart can be installed independently for existing clusters.

Known limitations / follow-ups:
- Remote_write support is limited to S3-compatible endpoints; we will improve secure credential rotation in a follow-up (ENG-4611).
- E2E tests use a lightweight TSDB retention to keep CI time small; we plan a longer-running soak test in the perf lab.

Related: Linear ENG-4532, SRE-210.
